specialRules.name: Power of the C'Tan
specialRules.text: Each model with the C'Tan Unit Type gains a Power of the C'Tan during the controlling player's Shooting Phase as the Active Player. When a model that can use the Powers of the C'Tan is selected to make a Shooting Attack during the Controlling Player's Shooting Phase, first roll a D6 and consult the following list of Powers of the C'Tan. This model may make a Shooting Attack using the weapon profile corresponding to the number rolled, in addition to any other Ranged Weapons it has. If a model using a Power of the C'Tan is a Vehicle, the Attack is made as if the Power of the C'tan was a Turret-mounted weapon.

specialRules.name: Æon Breach (X)
specialRules.text: When making Wound Tests or Armour Penetration Tests for Hits that have the Aeon Breach (X) special rule, if the result of any Dice rolled is equal to or greater than the value of X attached to the specific variant of this Special Rule then Invulnerable Saving Throws may not be made against that Attack.

specialRules.name: Automated Fortification
specialRules.text: A Fortification with this Special Rule may not be Captured and always remains under the Control of the Player that selected it, even if its Sub-Type would normally allow it to be Captured.

specialRules.name: Command Barge
specialRules.text:
If a Reaction is declared for a Unit that includes a majority of models with any variant of the Necron Trait, then the Controlling Player of the Reacting Unit may choose to make an Intelligence Check for any one Friendly Model with this special rule that is on the Battlefield (referred to as the 'Commanding Model'). The following modifiers are applied to the Commanding Model's Intelligence Check:
• If the Reacting Unit is not in Line of Sight of the Commanding Model, modify the result of the Check by +1.
• If all models in the Reacting Unit are more than 12" from the Commanding Model, modify the result of the Check by +2.
• If the Reacting Unit has the Reanimant Sub-Type, modify the result of the Check by -1.
If the Check is succesful then the Reaction Declared has its Reaction Point Cost reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 0). If the Check is failed then the Unit that includes the Commanding Model gains the Stunned Status.

specialRules.name: Dynastic Scion
specialRules.text: If a Model with this Special Rule is selected to fill a Command Slot in any Detachment in the Crusade Force Organisation Chart, then the Controlling Player may select one Apex Detachment instead of the Auxiliary Detachment usually granted by filling a Command Slot. However, no more than one Apex Detachment may be added to an army using the Dynastic Scion Special Rule. If an Apex Detachment is added to an Army using this Special Rule, the Model with this Special Rule counts as being a High Command Choice for the purposes of any version of the Slay the Warlord (X) Secondary Objective

specialRules.name: Entropic (X)
specialRules.text:
When making Wound Tests or Armour Penetration Tests for Hits that have the Entropic (X) special rule, if the result of any Dice rolled is equal to or greater than the value of X attached to the specific variant of this Special Rule then that Wound Test or Armour Penetration Test becomes an Entropic Strike. An Entropic Strike is automatically succesful, regardless of the Toughness Characteristic or Armour Value used to determine the Target Number, and causes a Wound or a Penetrating Hit as appropriate.

Entropic Strikes use the AP characteristic of the Weapon used to make the Attack, except against models with the Automata or Walker Unit Type. Against models with the Automata or Walker Unit Type only, Entropic Strikes are counted as having an AP characteristic of 2.

specialRules.name: Eternity Gate
specialRules.text:
In the controlling player's Movement Phase as the Active Player, when a Model with the Eternity Gate special rule has been selected, but either before or after it has been moved, the controlling player can choose one friendly unit entirely composed of models with the Reanimant Sub-Type that is on the Battlefield, in Reserves or Embarked on another Transport and which does not exceed the Eternity Gate Model's remaining Transport Capacity. Embark the chosen Unit upon the Model with the Eternity Gate. Any Enemy Units that become Unengaged as a result of the Unit being removed from the Battlefield may immediately Consolidate as described in the Aftermath Section of the Combat Resolution Sub-Phase. The Chosen Unit may still be selected as normal for that Movement Phase (meaning for instance that it can Disembark in the same turn it was transported, if it had not yet be selected).

If a model with the Eternity Gate special rule is Removed from Play, any Units that are Embarked upon it do not make an Emergency Disembarkation and no rule can inflict Hits to that Unit. The Unit is instead placed in Reserves.

specialRules.name: Ever-Living (X)
specialRules.text: A model with the Ever-Living (X) special rule gains an Ever-Living Damage Mitigation Test that can be used in Step 9 of the Shooting Attack process, Step 8 of the Initiative Step of the Fight Sub-Phase or Step 4 of the Challenge process to discard Wounds allocated to the model. A Damage Mitigation Test may be made after and in addition to a Saving Throw. The Target Number for an Ever-Living Damage Mitigation Test is the value of X attached to the specific variant of the Special Rule.

specialRules.name: Exile
specialRules.text:
When making a Wound Test for an attack with the Exile Special Rule, the Target's Initiative Characteristic is used instead of the its Toughness Characteristic. If the Attack Target has "-" listed instead of that Characteristic, the Wound Test automatically succeeds.

When making an Armour Penetration Test for an attack with the Exile Special Rule, add an additional D6 to the result of the Armour Penetration Test.

specialRules.name: Goad (X)
specialRules.text:
In the Controlling Player's Movement Phase as the Active Player, when a Model with the Goad (X) Special Rule has been selected, but either before or after it has been moved, the Controlling Player of that Model may activate this Special Rule. Once activated, the Controlling Player of the Model with the Goad (X) Special Rule (referred to as the 'Acting Model'), must select one friendly Unit within 6" of the Acting Model. The Unit selected (referred to as the 'Target Unit') must be entirely composed of Models with the Trait listed in Brackets as this Special Rule's variable. Once a Target Unit has been selected, the Player controlling the Acting Model must make an Intelligence Check for the Acting Model. If the Check is failed there is no further effect, but if the Check is passed then the Player controlling the Acting Model may select one of the following options:
• Push: All Models in the Target Unit gain +2 to their Movement Characteristic until the end of the Current Turn.
• Rouse: All Models in the Target Unit gain the Impact (A) Special Rule until the end of the Current Turn.
• Restrain: Remove one Tactical Status from the Target Unit.

The same Target Unit can be Goaded multiple times per turn. Each Target Unit can receive the Push and Rouse benefit only once per turn, but the Restrain benefit may be selected for the same Unit any number of times per turn.

specialRules.name: Gun Emplacement
specialRules.text: The hull of a Model with this Special Rule is only considered to be the central turret. The outriggers that form the gun carriage are ignored for all purposes.

specialRules.name: Hardwired for Destruction
specialRules.text: All Attacks, both melee and ranged, made by a model with the Hardwired for Destruction Special Rule gain the Critical Hit (6+) Special Rule. If an attack made by a model with the Hardwired for Destruction special rule already has a variant of the Critical Hit (X) special rule, then this special rule instead improves the X value associated with that attack's Critical Hit (X) special rule by 1 (for instance, from 6+ to 5+), to a maximum of Critical Hit (2+).

specialRules.name: Living Metal (X)
specialRules.text:
A model with this special rule does not make Repair Tests. Instead, during the Statuses Sub-Phase of the End Phase for a model with this special rule, the controlling player selects and apply one of the following to the model:
• Reconstruction Protocols – The model gains a number of Wounds or Hull Points equal to the value of X in the Living Metal (X) special rule variant possessed by the model. This cannot increase the model's Wounds or Hull Points above its starting value.
• Restoration Protocols – Remove a number of Statuses from the model equal to the value of X in the Living Metal (X) special rule variant possessed by the model.

specialRules.name: My Will Be Done (X)
specialRules.text: At the start of the Controlling Player's Turn as the Active Player, that Player can Activate the My Will Be Done (X) Special Rule of a Model with this Special Rule (referred to as the 'Commanding Model'). After this Special Rule has been Activated, the Controllling Player selects one Friendly Unit with the Reanimant Sub-Type within 6" of the Commanding Model to be the Target of this Special Rule. The Controlling Player takes a Willpower Check for the Commanding Model. If it is failed, nothing happens. If the Check is Succesful, the Player selects the Line (X) Special Rule or the Vanguard (X) Special Rule. Until the end of the Opposing Player's next Turn, the Target Unit gains that Special Rule, with a value of X equal to the value listed as part of the specific variant of the My Will Be Done (X) Special Rule. As long as the Target Unit has gained the Line (X) or Vanguard (X) Special Rule using the My Will Be Done Special Rule, all other Special Rules that Unit has that affects how Victory Points are scored are ignored and have no effect (including all other variants of the Line (X) or Vanguard (X) Special Rule, the Support Unit (X) Special Rule, the Heedless Special Rule, and any other similar Special Rule).

specialRules.name: Necrodermis
specialRules.text:
When a model with the Necrodermis Special Rule is allocated an unsaved Wound, the Damage Characteristic of the Unsaved Wound is halved, rounded up.

When a unit comprised entirely of models with the Necrodermis Special Rule would gain a Tactical Status, the controlling player can roll a D6 with a target number of '4+'. If succesful, the Unit does not gain the Tactical Status.

specialRules.name: Adamantium Will (X)
specialRules.text: A Model with the Adamantium Will (X) Special Rule gains an Adamantium Will Damage Mitigation Test that may be used to discard Wounds allocated to the Model, with a Target Number equal to the value of X listed in the specific variant of this Special Rule. An Adamantium Will Damage Mitigation Test may only be taken against Damage caused by Psychic Weapons, Psychic Powers, Psychic Reactions, Perils of the Warp, and Weapons with the Psychic or Immaterial Trait.

specialRules.name: Phase Motion
specialRules.text:
A unit that contains only models with this special rule suffers no penalty for moving or charging through Difficult Terrain, and automatically passes any Dangerous Terrain tests.

In addition, a unit that includes only models with this special rule may ignore the effects of any and all terrain it passes over during movement, including passing through vertical terrain and Impassable Terrain without penalty or restriction. However, such units may not begin or end their movement in Impassable Terrain.

specialRules.name: Ponderous
specialRules.text: A weapon that has the Ponderous special rule cannot be used to make a Shooting Attack when making a Shooting Attack as part of Volley Fire (even if the attacking Model has the Implacable Advance Special Rule), or in any situation in which the model would fire Snap Shots.

specialRules.name: Reanimation Beam (X)
specialRules.text:
In the Controlling Player's Movement Phase as the Active Player, when a model with the Reanimation Beam (X) Special Rule has been selected, but before or after it has been moved, the Controlling Player can Activate this Special Rule. Once Activated, the controlling player of the Model with the Reanimation Beam (X) special rule (referred to as the 'Acting Model') selects one friendly Unit with the Reanimant Trait within 18" of the Acting Model. Once a Target Unit has been selected, the Controlling Player makes a number of Resurrection (4+) Tests for the Target Unit equal to the value in brackets associated with the variant of the Reanimation Beam (X) Special Rule of the Acting Model.

If a model with the Reanimation Beam (X) Special Rule also has the Battlesmith (X) Special Rule, the model's Battlesmith (X) Special Rule may not be Activated in the same Phase as its Reanimation Beam (X) Special Rule and may target units within 12" of the Acting Model instead of 6".

specialRules.name: Retaliate
specialRules.text: Shooting Attacks made with a Weapon that has this Special Rule are always resolved as Snap Shots, unless the Attack was made as part of a Reaction.

specialRules.name: Reanimation Protocols (X)
specialRules.text: After removing Casualties from a Unit that includes Models with this Special Rule during Step 11 of the Shooting Attack Sequence or Step 10 of the Fight Sub-Phase, if any models with the Reanimation Protocols (X) Special Rule remain in the Unit, the Controlling Player makes a number of Resurrection (X) Tests this Unit equal to the number of models with the Reanimation Protocols (X) that have just been removed as casualties from the Unit. The value in brackets of the Resurrection Test is equal to the value in brackets associated with the Unit's specific variant of the Reanimation Protocols (X) Special Rule. Models returned to a Unit during a Fight Sub-Phase are returned the Initiative Step corresponding to their Combat Initiative and can Fight in the current phase, so long as that Initiative Step has not yet begun to be resolved. If the Initiative Step in which a Model would be placed has already been resolved, it cannot Fight in the current phase.

specialRules.name: Resurrection (X)
specialRules.text:
Certain special rules, reactions and pieces of wargear allow a player to make a number of "Resurrection" Tests for a unit. To make a Resurrection Test, the controlling player rolls a D6. If the result of the Dice is equal to or greater than the value X indicated in brackets as part of the specific variant of the Resurrection (X) special rule, one previously destroyed model is returned to the unit with 1 Wound remaining. The model must be placed in coherency with its unit and more than 1” from enemy models.

Only models with the Reanimant trait may be returned to units with a succesful Resurrection Test. Models with the Command sub-type may never be returned to the battlefield with a Resurrection Test, even if they also have the Reanimant trait.

Models that are returned to the battlefield with a succesful Resurrection Test are no longer counted as having been removed as casualties. Models returned to a Unit during a Fight Sub-Phase are returned to the Initiative Step corresponding to their Combat Initiative, so long as that Initiative Step has not yet begun to be resolved (this is an exception to the rule that states that models removed as casualties before their Initiative Step is resolved cannot attack).

specialRules.name: Scourge (X)
specialRules.text:
When making a Wound Test for an attack with the Scourge (X) Special Rule, the Characteristic indicated in brackets is used instead of the Target's Toughness Characteristic. If the Attack Target has "-" listed instead of that Characteristic, the Wound Test automatically fails.

When making an Armour Penetration Test for an attack with the Scourge (X) Special Rule, the Armour Value of the Target is used as normal, but any Penetrating Hits scored become Glancing Hits instead.

specialRules.name: Sentinel Protocols
specialRules.text: If all Automata Models in a unit have this special rule, that unit can be selected to make the Return Fire reaction and Overwatch Core Reaction and the Interceptor Advanced Reaction, ignoring the restrictions of the Automata sub-Type (any other restrictions to making Reactions still apply).

specialRules.name: Sleeping Sentry
specialRules.text:
When deploying a Model with this Special Rule before the start of the battle, the Controlling player may choose to deploy the Model anywhere on the Battlefield that is at least 12" from any point within the Opposing Player's Deployment Zone. A Model deployed this way is Dormant until the end of the Opposing Player's first Turn. The following rules apply to the model while it is Dormant:
• The Model is not counted as an Enemy Model, but instead as Impassible Terrain, for the purpose of deploying Units using any Special Rules that allow models to be deployed a certain distance away from Enemy Models. Enemy Units may still not be Deployed within 1" of the Model.
• The Model may not Move nor make a Shooting Attack.
• The Model Has a 3+ Invulnerable Save.

specialRules.name: Systematic Vigour
specialRules.text: While a Model with the [Crypto-Arkana] Sub-Type has joined a unit, all models with the Systematic Vigour Special Rule in that Unit receive a +1 bonus to their Weapon Skill and Attacks characteristic.

specialRules.name: Tesla (X)
specialRules.text: When making Hit Tests for Attacks that have the Tesla (X) special rule, if the result of any Dice rolled, before any modifiers are applied, is equal to or greater than the value of X attached to the specific variant of this special rule, then that attack causes 2 additional Hits in addition to the initial Hit, for a total of 3 Hits. Separate Wound Tests are made for each Hit caused this way. Additional Hits use the AP and Damage characteristics of the Weapon used to make the attack and retain any special rule that weapon had, but are not treated as a '6' for the purpose of any Rules that would be triggered on a certain result of a Hit Test – only the initial Hit does. If an Attack with the Tesla (X) Special Rule is made as Snap Shot, the Tesla (X) Special Rule only triggers on a To Hit roll of '6', regardless of the value of X associated with the variant of this Special Rule.

specialRules.name: The Will of the Phaeron
specialRules.text: While a Model with this special rule has joined a Unit, all Models with the Reanimant Trait in that Unit gain the Implacable Advance Special Rule.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Aetheric Thunder
powersOfTheCtan.text: 1: Aetheric Thunder. Weapon profile: R36, FP2, RS9, AP2, D2, Armourbane, Tesla (4+); Traits: Arc.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Antimatter Meteor
powersOfTheCtan.text: 2: Antimatter Meteor. Weapon profile: R36, FP1, RS8, AP4, D3, Barrage, Blast (7), Breaching (6+); Traits: –.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Cosmic Fire
powersOfTheCtan.text: 3: Cosmic Fire. Weapon profile: R H, FP1, RS7, AP4, D2, Hellstorm, Panic (2); Traits: Flame.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Seismic Assault
powersOfTheCtan.text: 4: Seismic Assault. Weapon profile: R36, FP15, RS6, AP4, D2, Pinning (2), Shock (Pinned); Traits: –.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Sky of Falling Stars
powersOfTheCtan.text: 5: Sky of Falling Stars. Weapon profile: R36, FP4, RS7, AP4, D3, Barrage, Blast (3), Pinning (2); Traits: Flame.

powersOfTheCtan.name: Time's Arrow
powersOfTheCtan.text: 6: Time's Arrow. Weapon profile: R36, FP1, RS10, AP2, D10, Aeon Breach (4+), Precision (2+); Traits: Entropic.
